title: Four Marian dogmas
hook: Mother of God, ever-virgin, Immaculate Conception, Assumption

segments.voice: Yesterday the social teaching block closed: love of neighbor, face to face and built into how we live. Your line was love made structural. Did you set up your ongoing act? Day one thousand three hundred twenty-seven.

An older woman in the hill country, expecting a child she never thought she'd have, hears someone at the door. It's Mary, her kinswoman, who has hurried there. And Elizabeth, in Luke's Gospel, cries out a question, in the Douay-Rheims: "And whence is this to me, that the mother of my Lord should come to me?" The mother of my Lord. Long after, the Church would sit with words like these and ask what exactly they mean. A new block of the path begins today: Mary, her feasts, her titles and her teaching. It starts with a word that can sound stiff and cold, and turns out to be neither. Today's word: dogma.
screen: `A KNOCK IN THE HILL COUNTRY.` → `THE MOTHER OF MY LORD.` → `A NEW BLOCK: MARY.`

segments.voice: First, the word. In the Catechism, a dogma is a truth the Church teaches as revealed by God, in a definitive way that asks for the assent of faith. The Catechism also gives it a gentle picture: dogmas are lights along the path of faith, making it safe. Not a fence. A row of lamps. Second, the four that concern Mary. One: Mother of God. A council at Ephesus affirmed for Mary the Greek title Theotokos, God-bearer, because the child she carried is one person, truly God and truly man. The title is first about who Jesus is. Two: ever virgin. Mary stayed a virgin before, during and after the birth of Jesus. Tomorrow takes that one slowly. Three: the Immaculate Conception. Pope Pius the Ninth taught that Mary, from the first moment of her own life, was kept free from original sin, by the grace of God and in view of what her son would do. It's about her conception, not Jesus' birth, an easy mix-up. Four: the Assumption. Pope Pius the Twelfth taught that at the end of her earthly life Mary was taken up, body and soul, into heavenly glory. Third, why the Church holds them together. Each one points back to Christ: who he is, how he came, what his saving work does, and where it leads. The Church sees in Mary what grace can do in one human life. Fourth, who holds what. Orthodox Christians also call Mary Theotokos and honor her as ever virgin, and celebrate her falling asleep and her glory. Other Christians hold some of these teachings and not others. This path describes the Catholic teaching, and ranks no one.
screen: `DOGMA: LIGHTS ALONG THE PATH.` · `MOTHER OF GOD, EVER VIRGIN.` · `IMMACULATE CONCEPTION, ASSUMPTION.` · `EACH ONE POINTS TO CHRIST.` · then, large: `THE MOTHER OF MY LORD.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: name the four. Settle, and breathe. On each slow breath, name one, and let a picture come with it. Mother of God: a mother holding a child. Ever virgin: a closed garden gate. Immaculate Conception: a clean first page. Assumption: someone lifted home. Go around the four again, slower. If one puzzles you, let it puzzle you; questions are welcome here. If you pray, you can greet Mary with Elizabeth's words, the mother of my Lord. The bell holds the time.
Dogma. A truth the Church teaches as revealed, defined so it can be held with confidence: lights along the path. Four of them concern Mary. Today's word.
Your line: four teachings. Today, try to name all four from memory once, before dinner: Mother of God, ever virgin, Immaculate Conception, Assumption. Day one thousand three hundred twenty-seven.

howItsDone: Catholics celebrate these teachings at feasts through the Church's year, including Mary, Mother of God, the Immaculate Conception and the Assumption, and the Hail Mary greets her as Mother of God.

fork.setup: you're at the council at Ephesus. what do you call Mary, whose child is truly God and truly man?
options: mother of Jesus' human nature only.
no title at all, to be safe.
fork.reveal: the council affirmed the title Theotokos, because her son is one person. the title protects a truth about Jesus first.

original.note: Greek: a decree or settled teaching; Acts uses it for the decisions of the apostles at Jerusalem.

trapdoor: what you thought: dogma means a rigid rule nobody may question.
what it means: a truth the Church teaches as revealed, held as a light on the path.
what a scholar hears: four Marian dogmas, each tied to Christ: Theotokos at Ephesus, perpetual virginity, and the two papal definitions of the Immaculate Conception and the Assumption.

notes: Editor pass: Ephesus now 'affirmed' rather than 'gave' Mary the title Theotokos (the title was in use before the council; CCC 466, 495); 'Catholics see' changed to 'The Church sees' to avoid speaking for all Catholics.
No years given for Ephesus or the definitions of 1854 and 1950, under the claims rule.
CCC 88 (definition of dogma) and 89 ('lights along the path of faith') paraphrased. Confirm.

Orthodox description: Theotokos, Ever-Virgin, and the Dormition; the script says they 'celebrate her falling asleep and her glory' and does not claim Orthodox acceptance of the Immaculate Conception or the dogmatic Assumption. Confirm fair.
'Other Christians hold some of these teachings and not others' is deliberately general; no count of Protestant positions.
Original: δόγμα; Acts 16:4 Greek has τὰ δόγματα for the Jerusalem decrees. Confirm.
Practice images (garden gate, clean page) are the script's own memory aids; the closed gate echoes a traditional reading of Ezekiel 44:2 but is not presented as such.
